passages.text: Hear this word, O house of Israel, this lamentation I take up against you: “Fallen is Virgin Israel, never to rise again. She lies abandoned on her land, with no one to raise her up.”
passages.sermon:
The prophet Amos speaks to the people of Israel.
He brings a message from God.
He says, “House of Israel, listen to this word.
I bring a lamentation against you.
Virgin Israel has fallen.
She will not rise again.
She lies abandoned on her own land.
No one will raise her up.”
passages.original: שִׁמְע֞וּ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֜י נֹשֵׂ֧א עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם קִינָ֖ה בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ נָֽפְלָה֙ לֹֽא־ תוֹסִ֣יף ק֔וּם בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נִטְּשָׁ֥ה עַל־ אַדְמָתָ֖הּ אֵ֥ין מְקִימָֽהּ׃

passages.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: “The city that marches out a thousand strong will only see a hundred return, and the one that marches out a hundred strong will have but ten left in the house of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He addresses the house of Israel.
A city may send out a thousand people.
Only one hundred will return.
A city may send out one hundred people.
Only ten will return.
This will happen to the house of Israel.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הָעִ֛יר הַיֹּצֵ֥את אֶ֖לֶף תַּשְׁאִ֣יר מֵאָ֑ה וְהַיּוֹצֵ֥את מֵאָ֛ה תַּשְׁאִ֥יר עֲשָׂרָ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: “Seek Me and live!
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the house of Israel.
The LORD commands them.
He says, "Seek Me."
He promises, "You will live."
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל דִּרְשׁ֖וּנִי וִֽחְיֽוּ׃

passages.text: Do not seek Bethel or go to Gilgal; do not journey to Beersheba, for Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to the house of Israel.
He gives a command.
Do not seek Bethel.
Do not go to Gilgal.
Do not cross over to Beersheba.
Gilgal will surely go into exile.
Bethel will become nothing.
Bethel will become a place of trouble.
passages.original: וְאַֽל־ תִּדְרְשׁוּ֙ בֵּֽית־ אֵ֔ל וְהַגִּלְגָּל֙ לֹ֣א תָבֹ֔אוּ וּבְאֵ֥ר שֶׁ֖בַע לֹ֣א תַעֲבֹ֑רוּ כִּ֤י הַגִּלְגָּל֙ גָּלֹ֣ה יִגְלֶ֔ה וּבֵֽית־ אֵ֖ל יִהְיֶ֥ה לְאָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: Seek the LORD and live, or He will sweep like fire through the house of Joseph; it will devour everything, with no one at Bethel to extinguish it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
He commands Israel.
Seek the LORD.
If you seek Him, you will live.
If you do not seek Him, He will come like fire.
He will sweep through the house of Joseph like fire.
The fire will devour everything.
No one at Bethel will be able to stop it.
passages.original: דִּרְשׁ֥וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה וִֽחְי֑וּ פֶּן־ יִצְלַ֤ח כָּאֵשׁ֙ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף וְאָכְלָ֥ה וְאֵין־ מְכַבֶּ֖ה לְבֵֽית־ אֵֽל׃

passages.text: There are those who turn justice into wormwood and cast righteousness to the ground.
passages.sermon:
Some people act with evil.
They change justice into bitterness.
They make justice like wormwood, which is bitter.
They throw righteousness down to the ground.
They reject what is right.
They do not honor righteousness.
passages.original: הַהֹפְכִ֥ים לְלַעֲנָ֖ה מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה לָאָ֥רֶץ הִנִּֽיחוּ׃

passages.text: He who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns darkness into dawn and darkens day into night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth— the LORD is His name— He flashes destruction on the strong, so that fury comes upon the stronghold.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is His name.
The LORD made the Pleiades.
The LORD made Orion.
The LORD turns darkness into dawn.
The LORD makes day become night.
The LORD calls for the waters of the sea.
The LORD pours the waters over the face of the earth.
The LORD brings destruction on the strong.
The LORD sends ruin upon the stronghold.
passages.original: עֹשֵׂ֨ה כִימָ֜ה וּכְסִ֗יל וְהֹפֵ֤ךְ לַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ צַלְמָ֔וֶת וְי֖וֹם לַ֣יְלָה הֶחְשִׁ֑יךְ הַקּוֹרֵ֣א לְמֵֽי־ הַיָּ֗ם וַֽיִּשְׁפְּכֵ֛ם עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ יְהוָ֥ה שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס הַמַּבְלִ֥יג שֹׁ֖ד עַל־ עָ֑ז וְשֹׁ֖ד עַל־ מִבְצָ֥ר יָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: There are those who hate the one who reproves in the gate and despise him who speaks with integrity.
passages.sermon: Some people hate a person who corrects others in public places.\r\nThese people despise anyone who speaks honestly.\r\nThey reject those who act with integrity.
passages.original: שָׂנְא֥וּ בַשַּׁ֖עַר מוֹכִ֑יחַ וְדֹבֵ֥ר תָּמִ֖ים יְתָעֵֽבוּ׃

passages.text: Therefore, because you trample on the poor and exact from him a tax of grain, you will never live in the stone houses you have built; you will never drink the wine from the lush vineyards you have planted.
passages.sermon:
You trample on the poor.
You take grain from the poor as a tax.
You build stone houses.
You will not live in those houses.
You plant beautiful vineyards.
You will not drink the wine from those vineyards.
passages.original: לָ֠כֵן יַ֣עַן בּוֹשַׁסְכֶ֞ם עַל־ דָּ֗ל וּמַשְׂאַת־ בַּר֙ תִּקְח֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ בָּתֵּ֥י גָזִ֛ית בְּנִיתֶ֖ם וְלֹא־ תֵ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֑ם כַּרְמֵי־ חֶ֣מֶד נְטַעְתֶּ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁתּ֖וּ אֶת־ יֵינָֽם׃

passages.text: For I know that your transgressions are many and your sins are numerous. You oppress the righteous by taking bribes; you deprive the poor of justice in the gate.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God knows their actions.
Their transgressions are many.
Their sins are numerous.
They oppress righteous people.
They take bribes.
They deprive poor people of justice at the city gate.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ רַבִּ֣ים פִּשְׁעֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲצֻמִ֖ים חַטֹּֽאתֵיכֶ֑ם צֹרְרֵ֤י צַדִּיק֙ לֹ֣קְחֵי כֹ֔פֶר וְאֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים בַּשַּׁ֥עַר הִטּֽוּ׃

passages.text: Therefore, the prudent keep silent in such times, for the days are evil.
passages.sermon:
The prudent person sees that these are evil days.
The prudent person chooses to keep silent.
The prudent person does not speak out at this time.
The prudent person knows that the times are full of trouble.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן הַמַּשְׂכִּ֛יל בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖יא יִדֹּ֑ם כִּ֛י עֵ֥ת רָעָ֖ה הִֽיא׃

passages.text: Seek good, not evil, so that you may live. And the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be with you, as you have claimed.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God is the God of Hosts.
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God commands you to seek good.
Do not seek evil.
If you seek good, you will live.
If you do this, the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be with you.
You have said that God is with you.
God will be with you if you seek good and not evil.
passages.original: דִּרְשׁוּ־ ט֥וֹב וְאַל־ רָ֖ע לְמַ֣עַן תִּֽחְי֑וּ וִיהִי־ כֵ֞ן יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־ צְבָא֛וֹת אִתְּכֶ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּֽם׃

passages.text: Hate evil and love good; establish justice in the gate. Perhaps the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.”
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD.
God is the God of Hosts.
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God commands the people.
Hate evil.
Love good.
Establish justice in the gate.
The gate is where leaders judge disputes.
If you do these things, God may show grace.
God may be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.
The remnant of Joseph means the remaining people of Israel.
passages.original: שִׂנְאוּ־ רָע֙ וְאֶ֣הֱבוּ ט֔וֹב וְהַצִּ֥יגוּ בַשַּׁ֖עַר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט אוּלַ֗י יֶֽחֱנַ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־ צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יוֹסֵֽף׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Hosts, the Lord, says: “There will be wailing in all the public squares and cries of ‘Alas! Alas!’ in all the streets. The farmer will be summoned to mourn, and the mourners to wail.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Hosts.  
The LORD is the Lord over all.  
The LORD says these words.  
There will be wailing in every public square.  
People will cry out, "Alas! Alas!" in every street.  
People will call the farmer to come and mourn.  
People will call the mourners to come and wail.
passages.original: לָ֠כֵן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י צְבָאוֹת֙ אֲדֹנָ֔י בְּכָל־ רְחֹב֣וֹת מִסְפֵּ֔ד וּבְכָל־ חוּצ֖וֹת יֹאמְר֣וּ הוֹ־ ה֑וֹ וְקָרְא֤וּ אִכָּר֙ אֶל־ אֵ֔בֶל וּמִסְפֵּ֖ד אֶל־ י֥וֹדְעֵי נֶֽהִי׃

passages.text: There will be wailing in all the vineyards, for I will pass through your midst,” says the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
The LORD says, "I will pass through your midst."
There will be wailing in all the vineyards.
passages.original: וּבְכָל־ כְּרָמִ֖ים מִסְפֵּ֑ד כִּֽי־ אֶעֱבֹ֥ר בְּקִרְבְּךָ֖ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Woe to you who long for the Day of the LORD! What will the Day of the LORD be for you? It will be darkness and not light.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God of Hosts.
He speaks to the people.
He warns those who desire the Day of the LORD.
He says, “Woe to you who long for the Day of the LORD.
Why do you want the Day of the LORD?
The Day of the LORD will not bring light.
The Day of the LORD will bring darkness.”
passages.original: ה֥וֹי הַמִּתְאַוִּ֖ים אֶת־ י֣וֹם יְהוָ֑ה לָמָּה־ זֶּ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם י֥וֹם יְהוָ֖ה הוּא־ חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא־ אֽוֹר׃

passages.text: It will be like a man who flees from a lion, only to encounter a bear, or who enters his house and rests his hand against the wall, only to be bitten by a snake.
passages.sermon:
The Day of the LORD will bring darkness and not light.
It will bring trouble and not safety.
A man may run away from a lion.
Then a bear will meet him.
He may enter his house to find safety.
He may rest his hand on the wall.
Then a snake will bite him.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָנ֥וּס אִישׁ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָאֲרִ֔י וּפְגָע֖וֹ הַדֹּ֑ב וּבָ֣א הַבַּ֔יִת וְסָמַ֤ךְ יָדוֹ֙ עַל־ הַקִּ֔יר וּנְשָׁכ֖וֹ הַנָּחָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Will not the Day of the LORD be darkness and not light, even gloom with no brightness in it?
passages.sermon:
The Day of the LORD is coming.
The Day of the LORD will not bring light.
The Day of the LORD will bring darkness.
The Day of the LORD will be full of gloom.
The Day of the LORD will have no brightness.
passages.original: הֲלֹא־ חֹ֛שֶׁךְ י֥וֹם יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹא־ א֑וֹר וְאָפֵ֖ל וְלֹא־ נֹ֥גַֽהּ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “I hate, I despise your feasts! I cannot stand the stench of your solemn assemblies.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God hates their feasts.
God despises their religious festivals.
God cannot stand the smell of their solemn gatherings.
passages.original: שָׂנֵ֥אתִי מָאַ֖סְתִּי חַגֵּיכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֥א אָרִ֖יחַ בְּעַצְּרֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Even though you offer Me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them; for your peace offerings of fattened cattle I will have no regard.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God sees their burnt offerings.
God sees their grain offerings.
God does not accept these offerings.
The people bring peace offerings of fattened cattle.
God does not look at these offerings.
God does not regard them.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ תַּעֲלוּ־ לִ֥י עֹל֛וֹת וּמִנְחֹתֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֣א אֶרְצֶ֑ה וְשֶׁ֥לֶם מְרִיאֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֥א אַבִּֽיט׃

passages.text: Take away from Me the noise of your songs! I will not listen to the music of your harps.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God commands them to stop their songs.
God calls their songs noise.
God refuses to listen to the music from their harps.
passages.original: הָסֵ֥ר מֵעָלַ֖י הֲמ֣וֹן שִׁרֶ֑יךָ וְזִמְרַ֥ת נְבָלֶ֖יךָ לֹ֥א אֶשְׁמָֽע׃

passages.text: But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God wants justice.
Justice must flow like a river.
God wants righteousness.
Righteousness must continue like a strong, never-ending stream.
passages.original: וְיִגַּ֥ל כַּמַּ֖יִם מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה כְּנַ֥חַל אֵיתָֽן׃

passages.text: Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the house of Israel.
God asks a question.
God says, “Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings?”
God refers to the forty years in the wilderness.
God addresses the people of Israel directly.
passages.original: הַזְּבָחִ֨ים וּמִנְחָ֜ה הִֽגַּשְׁתֶּם־ לִ֧י בַמִּדְבָּ֛ר אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: You have taken along Sakkuth your king and Kaiwan your star god, the idols you made for yourselves.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel made idols for themselves.
They made Sakkuth their king.
They made Kaiwan their star god.
They carried these idols with them.
They chose these gods for themselves.
passages.original: וּנְשָׂאתֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת סִכּ֣וּת מַלְכְּכֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת כִּיּ֣וּן צַלְמֵיכֶ֑ם כּוֹכַב֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם לָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Damascus,” says the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says this to Israel.
I will send you away.
I will send you far from here.
I will send you beyond Damascus.
You will go into exile.
passages.original: וְהִגְלֵיתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵהָ֣לְאָה לְדַמָּ֑שֶׂק אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־ צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃פ
